title: Effects of election — same diversity in both Schools (creation/fall as effects)
source_text: XXXI. Praeterea ex supra-dictis manifestum est, nec Ecclesiae Romanae, nec Ecclesiae Reformatae Doctores inter se convenire de effectis electionis, seu praedestinationis, dum in bonam partem sumitur. Etenim, prout antea nobis relatum est, variae sunt & discrepantes super hac re sententiae, tam in Schola Romana, quam in Schola Reformata. Eademque, aut fere eadem in isto negotio utrobique reperitur judiciorum & sensuum diversitas. Nam quemadmodum non pauci Scholae Reformatae Doctores ipsam creationem & lapsus permissionem numerant inter effectus praedestinationis quorundam ad salutem, idem quoque faciunt Theologi nonnulli Ecclesiae Romanae, ut praeter Estium, & Alphonsum Mendozam, aliosque supra memoratos, Dominicus Bannes in primam Thom. quaest. 23. ad secundum articulum, dubitatione secunda. Et sicut a plerisque Scholae Romanae Doctoribus istud negatur atque rejicitur, sic idem etiam negat & rejicit Doctorum Scholae Reformatae magna pars.
pass_a_gloss: Moreover from what has been said above it is manifest that neither the Doctors of the Roman Church nor those of the Reformed Church agree among themselves concerning the effects of election, or of predestination, when it is taken in the good part. For, as was related to us before, there are various and discrepant opinions on this matter, both in the Roman School and in the Reformed School. And the same, or nearly the same, diversity of judgments and senses is found on both sides in this business. For just as not a few Doctors of the Reformed School number creation itself and the permission of the fall among the effects of the predestination of certain men to salvation, so also do some Theologians of the Roman Church — as besides Estius and Alphonsus Mendoza and others mentioned above, Dominicus Bannes on the First Part of Thomas, question 23, at the second article, second doubt. And just as by most Doctors of the Roman School that is denied and rejected, so also the greater part of the Doctors of the Reformed School deny and reject the same.
pass_b_english: Neither Roman nor Reformed Doctors agree among themselves on election-effects.
Nearly the same diversity of judgment on both sides.
Some Reformed and some Romans (Estius, Mendoza, Báñez ST I.23 a.2) count creation & fall-permission as effects.
Most of each School deny and reject that count.
